summary: Split balance-history checkpoints into a required core artifact and an optional script-registry sidecar
details: The snapshot builder now emits independently hashed, signed, verified, and finalized core and script-registry SQLite artifacts from one sealed BTC checkpoint; the core database contains balances, live UTXOs, and block commitments but no script-registry table.

The standalone registry uses a frozen WITHOUT ROWID schema and has independent job, verification, completion, and failure state, so registry failure does not revoke an already completed core artifact.
Core artifacts always contain the complete live UTXO set, and both core and registry export reject a RocksDB workspace whose durable height differs from the sealed target.
Snapshot builder state and artifact manifests use the new split v1 contracts directly; legacy single-file builder jobs and artifacts are not accepted by the new tool.

The balance-history installer now requires a split v1 core manifest, verifies the artifact hash, SQLite integrity and schema, exact row counts, local consensus identity, latest block commitment, and staged state reference, then imports only balances, live UTXOs, and block commitments through a seven-stage atomic install.

Snapshot-installed RocksDB records strict core manifest, schema, state, and artifact provenance; the Docker completion marker is versioned and binds the core manifest digest, so legacy provenance and markers fail closed instead of entering a compatibility path.
Paired USDB indexer checkpoints now bind and verify the same split v1 core manifest and domain-separated Ed25519 signature payload, removing the remaining legacy single-file installation path.

Core installation no longer reads or imports script-registry rows, allowing balance-history startup as soon as the required core artifact is installed while optional registry-sidecar work proceeds independently.

Balance-history now resolves script hashes through a writable RocksDB overlay and an optional immutable SQLite base selected by a strict atomic active pointer; sidecar activation, lookup, integrity, or conflict failures remain isolated from core query and consensus readiness.

Registry readiness and resolve responses now expose explicit full-replay, snapshot-plus-sidecar, or post-snapshot-only coverage, and distinguish overlay/base hits, definitive misses, unresolved historical misses, and conflicts across the Rust client, CLI, control-plane, and console explorer.

The mainnet wrapper, object-storage publisher, release manifest, node installer, Compose runtime, status and doctor paths now use the split v3 release record directly; core remains the startup gate while registry acquisition and activation are independently observable and non-blocking.

Script-registry activation verifies the detached signature, full database hash, SQLite integrity, schema, metadata and exact row count before atomically publishing the active pointer; a failed replacement preserves the previous verified pointer, while explicit dry-run-first garbage collection protects every approved, selected or active artifact.
operator_actions: Use a new snapshot-builder root and regenerate split artifacts before publishing a release that contains this change; do not reuse legacy single-file builder state.

Install the generated core database together with its matching split v1 core manifest; existing single-file snapshot markers or snapshot-installed RocksDB data must be replaced for this development-stage format change.
Regenerate and republish a split v3 snapshot release record before enabling snapshots in a new release; the checked-in legacy v2 record is intentionally no longer selected.
Use usdb-node status or doctor to inspect optional registry state, and review the dry-run output before invoking usdb-node snapshot gc --confirm.
